note: *um chifre de salvação*, as 17:3c; the blind reader found *chifre* puzzling or slang. MS1932 and the CNBB explain it (*força*, *poderoso Salvador*), both options.
*desde os tempos antigos*: all three v1 readers objected to the row's *a sǽculo → desde sempre* said of prophets (heard as eternal prophets). A departure from that row when said of people.
*o saber da salvação*: the stylist found it academic, the blind reader briefly heard *sabor*. *o conhecimento* (MS1932, the Diurnal) is the *sciéntia* row's named option.
*o Oriente do alto*: the Latin's word and the Vulgate's Messianic name; the blind reader heard the East. MS1932 and the CNBB say *o Sol nascente*.
*para o caminho da paz* keeps the Latin's motion *in viam*; MS1932, the Diurnal and the CNBB all have the familiar *no caminho da paz*.
